summary: The flow takes an attacker-influenced random int in CWE789_Uncontrolled_Mem_Alloc__random_HashMap_66a.bad(), passes it via an int array to badSink() in the 66b class, and uses it directly as a HashMap initial capacity. A negative value throws IllegalArgumentException and an excessively large value triggers uncontrolled memory allocation (OOM). The fix adds a bounds check in badSink so the capacity is only used when it falls within a sane, non-negative range, preserving the HashMap-sizing feature for all valid inputs.
